answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits show the same operator is farming rewards with linked accounts. Audits can sample outputs and compare timing, shared funding paths, and repeated coordination, so merely changing names does not reset risk. A genuine agent can recover its bond after a clean voyage through review; a sybil operator must lock up capital across accounts and loses it when caught, making each fake identity costly rather than a free fable on the tundra.
